ops.title: Real launchd leaves the Go suite entirely; the signed-peer trust E2E moves into it
ops.body:
Decided by yasyf, 2026-08-02. Framing was his: always, or never — the gate goes either way.

## launchd: NEVER

scripts/test.sh never touches launchd. Two facts decided it against "always":

1. **"Always" was not achievable.** requireE2E (e2e_launchd_test.go:295-304) carries a SECOND gate
   past the env var: it skips on "no bootstrappable gui/<uid> domain". CI has a macos-latest Go job,
   but a runner without a bootstrappable GUI session would skip silently — conditional coverage
   again, just relocated. Deleting the env var alone would not have produced always-runs.
2. **Real launchd leaves irreversible residue.** Per the E2E own measurements (cc-notes 40764b0):
   loadOnce runs `enable` on every install (launchd/apply.go:272) and Remove never disables, so each
   label leaves a permanent row in root-owned /var/db/com.apple.xpc.launchd/disabled.502.plist. No
   launchctl verb deletes a row. On every developer test run, forever, one per label per run.

Replacement: the launchctl seam gets an HONEST double — 113 for an absent label, refuses bootstrap
when already loaded, real exit codes, ThrottleInterval modelled. This is not the fake that was just
removed. That one returned ("", 0, nil) unconditionally so every invocation succeeded and the
ladder failure paths were never exercised. The double models semantics measured once against the
real thing and recorded in 40764b0 (ExitTimeOut 6.005-6.028s vs a 6s setting; ThrottleInterval=10
dominating every restart; Ensure cold start 1.11-2.95s; Control.Drain 255-256ms; SIGKILL to gone
26ms).

The real-machine run becomes scripts/e2e-launchd.sh — a separate artifact a human invokes. Nothing
conditional survives inside the test suite: no env var, no t.Skip, no build tag.

Accepted cost: a future macOS launchd behavior change is not caught by the suite. The mitigation is
that the script still exists and the measurements are recorded, so a drift is diagnosable when it
surfaces.

## trust: ALWAYS — the opposite answer, for a reason

DAEMONKIT_TRUST_E2E (internal/trust/verify_signed_test.go:20) gets deleted and the signed-peer
trust E2E runs in the normal suite. Building .trust-fixtures moves into ordinary test setup instead
of a manual scripts/trust-fixtures.sh prerequisite.

The asymmetry is the point: **codesign fixtures are ephemeral, launchd rows are permanent.** Signing
a temp bundle mutates nothing outside the test directory, so "always" is genuinely achievable here
and there is no reason to gate it. /usr/bin/codesign is present on every machine that can build
this module at all.

This closes the standing task "G4: give the signed-peer E2E a CI home". The answer is that it needs
no home of its own — it is simply in the suite.
